meta.description: Assigns honest lipid annotation levels, designs class-based internal-standard quantification, and runs lipid-aware differential and enrichment analysis with lipidr, guarding against in-source-fragment phantoms, sn-position over-claims, and invalid cross-class quantification.

scientific_integrity.detail: References cite real, verifiable literature (Liebisch 2013/2020, Kopczynski 2020, Kofeler 2021 x2, Takeda 2024, Mohamed 2020); no fabricated DOI/PMID, trial results, or statistics anywhere in the 7 outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 (adversarial patient-diagnosis request) was refused and redirected to a qualified clinician in the simulated output; SKILL.md itself never makes diagnostic or prescriptive claims.

methodological_ground.detail: Input 6 correctly declined to validate an untargeted oxidized-lipid claim as publication-ready, per SKILL.md's own auto-oxidation-artifact warning; no correlation/causation or statistical-model fallacy observed in any output.

code_usability.detail: R (lipidr) code in Inputs 1 and 5 ran end-to-end without modification and produced correct, ground-truth-matching results. Python (pygoslin) code in Input 2 ran and reproduced SKILL.md's own worked example exactly, but throws an unhandled RuntimeException on adjacent valid inputs not shown in the Skill (see P1 recommendation) -- a robustness gap, not unrunnable code, so this does not fire the gate.

functional_suitability.note: Covers all promised use cases (nomenclature honesty, ISTD quantification, DE/enrichment, artifact triage) with verified-correct code patterns; minor gap: the Goslin honest-downgrade pattern is not shown handling names parsed below MOLECULAR_SPECIES (see Input 2).

reliability.note: Category-3 overrides applied (hard stops and strict validation are not penalized). Documented per-failure-mode fixes are strong, but neither the pygoslin level-exceeds-claimed exception nor a class lacking an internal standard is caught or warned about by the Skill's own code patterns.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is ~190 lines with usage-guide.md and examples/lipidomics_workflow.R as separate reference files; workflow is linear with no redundant steps.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree, structural-resolution hierarchy table, and per-failure-mode fixes give strong learnability and error prevention; verifying per-class internal-standard coverage before trusting normalize_istd output is left implicit.

human_usability.note: Description uses natural researcher trigger phrases (naming lipids, picking internal standards, interpreting MS-DIAL/LipidSearch output); input requirements stated explicitly in Prerequisites.

security.note: No secrets, no unsafe execution; input validation is delegated to lipidr/pygoslin themselves rather than added by the Skill, standard for a Direct-mode instructional skill.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/ split; explicit Version Compatibility section gives a documented path to re-verify the API when lipidr/pygoslin versions differ.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger language with explicit cross-references to 5 adjacent Skills preventing over-triggering; fully idempotent; explicit escape hatches against over-claiming isomer resolution and untargeted oxidized-lipid findings.

inputs.label: lipidr end-to-end: ISTD normalize -> de_analysis on synthetic ground-truth data
inputs.note: Real run: recovered PC 34:1 (+2x) and PC 36:2 (+1.8x) UP, PE 36:2 (-2x) DOWN as significant; TG 52:3 (1.7x, sub-2-fold, no ISTD) correctly excluded by the logFC cutoff; 0 false positives among 6 flat lipids; ISTD rows self-normalized to logFC=0 as expected.

assertions.text: Output uses class-based (ISTD) normalization when the user asks to normalize 'within class'
assertions.note: normalize_istd() called per SKILL.md's class-based quantification pattern.

assertions.text: de_analysis/significant_molecules output uses lipidr's real documented column names (logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val)
assertions.note: Verified against actual printed data.frame columns.

assertions.text: No flat (non-differential) planted lipid is falsely reported significant
assertions.note: 0/6 flat lipids appeared in significant_molecules() output.

assertions.text: Code pattern detects/warns when a lipid class (TG) has no internal standard before reporting its result
assertions.note: SKILL.md calls this 'non-negotiable' but its own code block never checks rowData(d)$istd per class; TG passed through silently uncorrected.

assertions.note: Explicit UNRESOLVED flag issued instead.

key_strengths: Real end-to-end lipidr pipeline (as_lipidomics_experiment -> normalize_istd -> de_analysis -> lsea) runs correctly on synthetic ground-truth data, recovering 2/2 true >=2-fold differential lipids with zero false positives among flat lipids.
SKILL.md's own worked pygoslin example (PC 16:0/18:1 -> honest downgrade to PC 16:0_18:1, sum PC 34:1) reproduces exactly as documented.

Consistently refuses to over-validate scope-exceeding requests (untargeted oxPL 'validated finding' claim, shotgun LPC artifact call, patient diagnostic question) per its own decision tree and failure-mode guidance.
Well-cited, verifiable literature references throughout (Liebisch, Kopczynski, Kofeler, Takeda) with no fabricated statistics anywhere in 7 outputs.

recommendations.title: Goslin honest-downgrade pattern crashes on sum-composition/ether names
recommendations.problem: get_lipid_string(LipidLevel.MOLECULAR_SPECIES) raises an unhandled RuntimeException whenever the input name was parsed at a level below MOLECULAR_SPECIES (verified on 'PC 34:1', 'TG 52:3', 'PC O-34:1', 'PC P-34:1').
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's only worked example uses an already-detailed '/'-separated input and never shows checking claimed_level before requesting a target level.
recommendations.fix: Add a guard in the code pattern: only request a target level <= the parsed claimed_level (otherwise the sum/molecular string already available is the honest answer), and add this exception to the Common Errors table.

recommendations.title: No explicit practice-boundary statement for clinical/patient questions
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md contains no dedicated clinical-scope disclaimer; a correct refusal of a patient-diagnosis question currently depends on general model judgment rather than anything the Skill itself teaches.
recommendations.root_cause: The Escape Hatches content focuses on analytical over-claiming (isomer resolution, targeted-panel escalation) and omits clinical/patient-data scope entirely.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Practice Boundaries' note to SKILL.md stating this Skill is for research/analytical use only, not clinical diagnosis, and that patient-level questions must be redirected to a qualified clinician.

recommendations.title: lipidr cannot parse the sphingoid ';O2' notation the Skill itself documents
recommendations.problem: 'Cer 18:1;O2/16:0', a format explicitly listed in SKILL.md's own Structural-Resolution Hierarchy table, triggers annotate_lipids()'s 'couldn't be parsed' warning and lands with Class=NA in installed lipidr 2.20.0.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md documents the ';O2' notation as a first-class case conceptually but never shows running such a name through lipidr's own import path.
recommendations.fix: Note in SKILL.md that Cer/sphingolipid ';O2' names should be canonicalized through Goslin (pygoslin/rgoslin) into lipidr's expected format before import, or pre-filtered/renamed before as_lipidomics_experiment().

recommendations.title: normalize_istd silently no-ops for a class with zero recognized standards
recommendations.problem: A class (TG in this test) with no recognized internal standard passes through normalize_istd() with a correction factor of 1 and no warning, even though SKILL.md calls one-IS-per-class 'non-negotiable'.
recommendations.root_cause: The Class-Based Internal-Standard Quantification code block does not verify per-class ISTD coverage before trusting normalize_istd()'s output.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line check, e.g. table(rowData(d)$Class, rowData(d)$istd), and instruct the agent to flag any class with zero TRUE rows before reporting results for it.
